Municipality of Alburquerque Province of Bohol Dear VM Doria, Jr.: 6.0. 54 S. 2Diß This has reference to your letter dated 30 October 2017 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on the following issues, which we quote in toto, viz: 3. Legality of the ordinance (Municipal Ordinance No. 1, S.2008, otherwise known as the "Solid Waste Management Code) being used as basis for the cluster sanitary landfill; Legality of the supplemental Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) entered into and by the additional cluster member-municipalities with the former Mayor Efren Tungol wherein the latter had no authority from the Sangguniang Bayan to enter into such agreement; What is the role of the Provincial Cluster Board as far as accepting of additional municipalities as members of the cluster sanitary landfill, and in this case, what is also the role of the Sangguniang Bayan. on lhe issues: Foremost, it is understood that the herein subject ordinance refers to a "Municipal Ordinance", hence, it covers only the whole municipality of Alburquerque, Bohol and cannot be made effective for the cluster of municipalities, unless it was clearly stated therein that it is the intention of the ordinance. Nevertheless, this Department has reservation on giving its legal opinion on the matter, unless, we be furnished with a copy of the subject Municipal Ordinance, so that we can properly evaluate the same. In addition, issues no. 2 and 3 in your letter can be threshed out only by said ordinance. However, since this ordinance was approved on 2008, the same is presumed valid and this Department is without authority to rule on the validity/invalidity thereof as this is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts.

Assuming [hat the herein ordinance does not embrace the intention of the LGU of Albuquerque, Bohol, you always have the option to amend the same. As to the legality of the supplemental MOA, It must be understood that a MOA is a form of a contract, therefore, must comply with Section 22(c) of the Local Government Code, to wit: "Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. " On the basis of the above-quoted provision, it is clear that, before the mayor could sign the NIOA, there must be an authorization from the sanggunian. Nevertheless, we emphasized that pursuant to the Department's Memorandum Order No. 2010-021, dated 17 September 2017, this Department was advised not to act on queries involving presumptively valid acts, such as but not limited to, enacted ordinances and consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of public officer concerned. Thus, we believe that the comments provided by Region VII is usefUl not to this forum but in the court when the validity of the ordinance will be attacked/ questioned. Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. Effectivity is governed by Section 59(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: (a) Unless 'Section 59. " Based on Section 59(a) of the LGC, an ordinance of a local government unit becomes efléctive as of the date the framers of such ordinance would like it to be effective and in the absence of such effectivity clause, the same shall take effect after ten (IO) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. Accordingly, Ordinance No. I, S.2008, otherwise known as the "Solid Waste Management Code 't as a matter of course, be already given legal effect and implemented even if the same is still pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Validity on the other hand, refers to the substantive requirement of an ordinance, whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws. The pertinent provision of the LGC provides that: "Section 5b. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panla/a wigan. dap Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panla/awigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public in vestment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within aperiod often (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang pan]alavvigan in making its decision. (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlala wigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken.

As discussed above, pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the Ordinance under review is already effective and can be given full force and eftéct upon the arrival of the time provided for in the effectivity clause of the ordinance. Premises given, the Department, in its previous legal opinions, has been very consistent that inasmuch as the ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment under the Local Government Code, the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice.2 Any issues or questions thereon as to the substantive validity and enforceability of an ordinance should be threshed out by filing a judicial declaration of nullity of ordinance before the proper court3. Alternatively, if adequate relief is not available through other existing forms of actions or proceedings, a special civil action för declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Section I and Section 4, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court may also be resorted to, to wit: "Section 1.
